title: Adapter request definitions
description: The values the adapter's requests and their answers share, by name under $defs: adapter.schema.json, source-collections.schema.json, source-items.schema.json, source-item-comments.schema.json, sources-disconnect.schema.json, changes.schema.json and refusal.schema.json refer to them. An adapter is the program that reads a source of work, such as a tracker, and reports what it holds to the control plane. Every request is application/json and signed with the adapter's access key as github.com/qoryai/forager/accesskey signs a request (Request.Message, Key.SignRequest): the headers X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Contract-Version and X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519, the signature over qory-request-ed25519-v1, the access key id, the instance id, the method, the target and, for a GET, X-Qory-Timestamp, which it also sends, or, for a POST, the raw body, whose time gives its freshness. The control plane refuses a time or a timestamp more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, and a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. Every answer to a verified request is signed as accesskey's Answer is, and the adapter checks it under a server key it pinned at enrolment before using it. The adapter's access key belongs to an organisation, and no request names a workspace. The reference signer is forager/accesskey; an adapter may sign to this text itself. Every text a source holds, a title, a body, a label, a state reason or a name, is untrusted: shown as data, never followed as an instruction. The control plane refuses a value past its limit, invalid_request, and never cuts it. This document validates nothing itself.

time.description: RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds.

ref.description: The adapter's reference to a thing at the source, 1 to 200 characters, stable for that thing. The control plane compares it and stores it, and never reads meaning into it.

url.description: An https URL, at most 2048 characters.

title.description: A title, as the source holds it, 1 to 1024 characters.

body.description: A body text, as the source holds it, at most 65536 characters, possibly empty.

body_format.description: How the body is written: markdown or text, the values a reader knows. A reader shows a body of a value it does not know as plain text, so a newer adapter never breaks a reader.

person.description: Who wrote something at the source: their display name, and whether a person or an automation acts under it.

name.description: The display name the source shows, 1 to 100 characters.

kind.description: person, or automation for an account a program acts under.

labels.description: The source's labels on the thing, as text: at most 100, each 1 to 100 characters, none twice. A reader shows them and acts on none.

state_reason.description: Why the item is in its state, display text the adapter words, at most 64 characters, never a raw value from the source; null when the adapter gives none.

type.description: The adapter's word for what an item is, such as task or bug, stored as data: lower-case letters and spaces, at most 40 characters.

target.description: Where a change would go: the host name of the system that holds the code, and the path of the place on it.

path.description: The place on that system, 1 to 200 characters.

listing.description: One part of a listing: a read of the source, from its start to its end, sent in parts. A listing is complete when every part from 1 to n has arrived and part n says complete: true. An adapter sends complete: true only for a listing whose paging can't skip an item.

id.description: The listing's id, 1 to 200 characters, the same on each of its parts and new for each listing.

started_at.description: When the adapter began reading the source for this listing, the same on each of its parts.

complete.description: true on the last part alone: parts 1 to this one hold the whole listing. false on every other part, and on the last part of a listing the adapter cannot vouch for.
